question.text: Anita is 30 years old and wants to accumulate Rs.5 crore by age 60. If she expects an annual return of 12% (monthly compounding), approximately how much should she invest monthly through SIP?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the standard FV/PMT future-value-of-an-annuity approach from Series X-A: with FV = Rs.5 crore, n = 360 months and i = 1% per month (12% p.a. monthly compounded), the required monthly SIP works out to roughly Rs.14,300. Series XVII gives a comparable example where Rs.5,000 per month at 12% for 30 years grows to about Rs.1.747 crore, which scales consistently with this answer. The Trap: Rs.28,000 roughly corresponds to a much lower expected return, Rs.42,000 to an even lower one, and Rs.7,000 understates the requirement; the power of compounding over 30 years explains why the monthly contribution is relatively modest. Note: Use the FV/PMT formula (or a financial calculator) for monthly SIP sizing — generic shortcuts like the Rule of 72 estimate doubling time, not the monthly contribution needed for a target corpus.
